topic: What if you got the GTA6 hospital bill in real life?

script.text: It starts on a Saturday morning, after a very long night with a controller in your hand. You trip on the stairs, and the world blinks grey. When it comes back, you're outside City General, three streets away, in your pyjamas. Perfectly fine. A nurse stares at you. Then your phone buzzes. Your first bill: two thousand, nine hundred and nine dollars, for falling down the stairs. You fall down a few more things that morning, on purpose this time. That's how you figure out the rules.
Rule one: you can't die. Whatever happens, you blink, and you're back at the hospital doors, healed.

Rule two: the bill is real. Every line is the real price of what just happened to you, at real American hospital prices, as if you had to recover the normal way. A broken leg gets billed like a broken leg, even if it heals in a blink.
Rule three: the bill only ever comes to you. Nobody else pays a cent.
By ten in the morning, the number at the top of your phone says sixty-three thousand, three hundred and twenty dollars. You have eleven dollars in your bank account. And it's only Saturday.
